notes:
Account summary
- Prospect is evaluating Redwood Private (AWS VPC) for internal knowledge assistant + customer support summarization. Strong preference for Private deployment vs hosted API due to data handling + network controls.
- Environment: AWS, multi-account. VPCs are centrally managed; app teams consume shared networking patterns (TGW, centralized egress proxy). They will provision a dedicated “Redwood Private” account but must comply with corp network baselines.

Key requirements (networking)
- Strict egress control: “No open internet egress.” Security wants private-only connectivity wherever possible. They are okay with egress proxy / centralized NAT only if explicitly justified and logged.
- Prefer zero public subnets. If any public resources are required, they want a clear explanation + compensating controls.
- Private DNS: they use Route53 Resolver (inbound/outbound) + private hosted zones. Need modules to integrate cleanly (no surprise public DNS dependencies).
- Endpoints: asked for a definitive list of AWS VPC endpoints required for installer/runtime operations. They specifically called out ECR (api + dkr), S3 (gateway), CloudWatch Logs, and STS. Optional: SSM if preflight tooling uses it.
- Existing network constraints: shared transit gateway, forced DNS forwarding, and “deny by default” egress SGs/NACLs (they don’t want Redwood modules to hardcode NACL opinionation).

Security / compliance requirements
- Audit logging is mandatory:
  - VPC Flow Logs enabled at VPC level.
  - Log routing preference: S3 in centralized log archive account (preferred) OR CloudWatch Logs with subscription filter to SIEM.
  - Retention controls: minimum 365 days (policy driven). They want retention configurable.
- Encryption hooks: require KMS CMK for logs (Flow Logs to CWL/S3) and any Terraform-created log groups/buckets.
- Access controls: least-privilege IAM guidance for Terraform apply role + change control artifacts. They asked for a “permissions checklist” they can hand to their IAM team.

Product fit notes
- They reacted positively to the alpha Terraform modules concept (“reference baseline we can bless once, then reuse”). Biggest concern is whether the modules support their locked-down pattern without becoming a fork.
- They want a supported/validated topology matrix (private-only endpoints/no NAT vs centralized egress vs per-AZ NAT) and explicit non-supported combos.

- 2026-02-10 (Fireflies ff-88312): Technical deep dive. Network team asked for: required endpoints list + whether installer needs STS/SSM; request for a minimal terraform example that works without public egress.
- 2026-02-14: Shared internal stub links to endpoint requirements matrix + pilot plan.

Pilot plan (proposed)

  - Target pattern: isolated/private subnets + interface endpoints + S3 gateway endpoint + private DNS enabled.
  - Egress: start with “private-only” (no IGW) and document any required exceptions.
- Phase 2: Run redwood-private-installer networking preflight checks; validate endpoint reachability and DNS.
- Success metric they care about: “time from account ready → installer can pull images and bootstrap control plane” (they quoted 3-4 weeks historically; want <1 week).

- Provide them an explicit endpoint policy recommendation (at least stub) so they can align with their security team (they do not allow ‘*’ service principals without review).
- Share IAM permissions summary for Terraform apply + any runtime roles needed.
